as_told.title: Ning Li's superconductor weight loss results

plain: A scientist named Ning Li, working at the University of Alabama in Huntsville under a man named Larry Smalley, is said to have studied making objects lighter using superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance when very cold. Michels says she published, with credit to a colleague named Douglas Torr, that the masses she tested lost between 0.5% and 2.1% of their weight across several trials, and the story has her later starting a company around the work. Michels tells it himself on two episodes, without naming a source, and if the result held up it would be a first step toward controlling gravity.
